question: What evidence does Aquino (2025) provide about aquatic taxa in Pampanga aquaculture areas, and what prevents using it as wild-waterway fish coverage?

source.citation: Aquino, D. R. S. (2025). Risk Assessment of Introduced Species in the Aquaculture Areas of Pampanga, Philippines. Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Biology & Fisheries, 29(3), 311–324. https://doi.org/10.21608/ejabf.2025.426853.
source.bibliographicCrosscheck: The publisher PDF title page and EBSCO catalog record identify Divine Reine S. Aquino alone; running page headers read “Lansang & Aquino, 2025.” No additional author identity was inferred.

studyScope.samplingDescription: The methods say 404 respondents were selected as 10% of fishpond operators on municipal agriculture-office lists. The respondent-site sentence names Arayat, Candaba, Minalin, Macabebe and Masantol but omits Magalang even though Magalang is listed as a freshwater risk-assessment zone.
studyScope.waterbodyType: Commercial aquaculture ponds and operator-reported links to nearby waters; not a standardized open-water fish survey.
studyScope.studyDates: No field sampling or interview dates were found in the reviewed article text.

methodsAndLimitations.interviews: Structured face-to-face questionnaire asked about potential invasive species in aquaculture ponds and their biological profiles.
methodsAndLimitations.specimens: Article says potential invasive aquatic specimens were collected with local residents using their capture methods and submitted to the National Museum of the Philippines for identification; the reviewed article provides no specimen catalogue or accession identifiers.
methodsAndLimitations.riskScreen: Experts completed AS-ISK basic and climate-change screening. The resulting “high risk” classifications are potential-invasiveness assessments, not legal designations, abundance estimates, fishery catchability or confirmation of wild occurrence.
methodsAndLimitations.geography: No station/pond coordinates, verified waterbody boundary, river-reach crosswalk, or fish-by-waterbody voucher matrix is supplied in the reviewed text.
reportingIssues: Study-area criteria name six municipalities but the methods paragraph that describes 404 respondents names only five, omitting Magalang.
The text says four finfish species were found at all sites but the sentence names only Channa striata, Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus and Clarias batrachus.
The article’s conclusion says “six fish species,” although its six risk-screened aquatic taxa include the softshell turtle Pelodiscus sinensis.
The table text extraction collapses the municipality columns and several source-name rows; no site-level taxon assignments were reconstructed from ambiguous layout.

sourceReportedRiskTaxa.interpretation: Names included in the article’s six-taxon AS-ISK risk screen, not a validated wild-waterway occurrence roster.

riverAndWetlandInterpretation.authorReportedConnections: The discussion attributes some fishpond entry to irrigation canals and mentions the Pasig-Potrero River, Candaba flood-control area, Magalang River and Arayat River. These are interview/narrative pathways; the methods do not report sampling fish from those rivers or the wetland itself.
riverAndWetlandInterpretation.decision: Use this as a research-only aquaculture and invasive-risk lead. Do not project fishpond reports onto the Pampanga River, Pasig-Potrero River, Magalang River, Arayat River, Candaba wetland, or any mapped waterbody.

rights.itemSpecificReuseLicense: Not found in the reviewed publisher PDF or article metadata.
rights.handling: Retain attribution and short factual summaries only; do not reproduce the source table, figure, risk-screen questionnaire, or photographs without permission.

nextAction: Continue separate, site-resolved evidence collection for the named river, wetland, and lake systems. If using these pond reports later, request the underlying anonymized specimen-to-pond crosswalk, field dates, National Museum accession identifiers, and item-specific reuse terms. Keep aquaculture, wild occurrence, risk screening, and fishing advice as separate data types.

sources.supports: Publisher-hosted 2025 full text: named freshwater/brackish aquaculture assessment zones, operator-interview method and 404 respondent count, resident-assisted specimen collection and National Museum identification statement, the six AS-ISK taxa, author-reported pond/riverside context, and article reporting inconsistencies. EBSCO catalog metadata cross-check for the DOI and author-list discrepancy.
